_note: What Grandma Tome says when the farmer talks to them (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; the gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction (gift_birthday on their birthday); gift_items names their own answer to a keepsake or a dish (Talk.gift_line), by item or by dish: / keepsake:<reaction> (gifts in data/villagers/tome.json). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Eighty-one autumns today, and still the persimmons ripen on time. Thank you, child.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A present, on my birthday? You'll make an old woman cry in the street.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Still here? Don't mind me, I'm only resting my knees.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Go on, the field won't hoe itself. I'll be here.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I put you in my last letter again. My son wrote back that he'd like to meet you, come New Year.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The persimmon by the shrine has more buds than last year. I counted them, twice.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Come in for tea whenever the lamp's lit. You needn't knock. Family doesn't knock.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: When you walk by, the morning feels a little longer. In a good way.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My husband used to keep that field, you know. He'd be glad to see it green.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I made too much pickled radish again. Come by the house when you're hungry.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You've the same habit he had. Looking at the sky before you look at the soil.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Cold enough to crack the water jar. Wrap your neck, child.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Winter is for mending baskets and waiting. The ground needs its sleep too.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh, good morning. You're the one who took the old farm up the hill?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I come to the shrine every morning. At my age, you say thank you early.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Hm? Ah, the new farmer. The path gets muddy by the pond. Mind your step.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Young people don't stay long in this village. Let's see about you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: On Sundays I walk round the shrine twice. Once for me, once for him.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The plum by my house has opened. Spring always comes in quietly here.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Sow the turnips before the rains. That's what my mother told me.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: This heat... Drink water before you're thirsty. And wear a hat.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Listen to the cicadas. In my day we counted them to fall asleep.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The persimmons are turning. Soon the whole hill smells sweet.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Harvest time. Everyone is busy, and the evenings come in early.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The pond is calm today. Days like this are a gift.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My knees say rain tomorrow. They're right more often than the radio.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: When the butterbur buds push up on the bamboo hill, I know spring has really come. Pick them small, before they open.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The wild raspberries are ripe on the hill. I used to send the children up with a basket. Back came an empty basket and red mouths.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Chestnuts are falling on the hill. Mind the burrs. And look near the top, under the pines. Something rare grows there, if you're lucky.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Even under snow, the old stumps on the hill keep a few enoki. The old folk got through winter by knowing where to look.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: For me? Oh my... this is just what I like.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Thank you, child. I'll make tea and think of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: How kind. I'll put it to good use, thank you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh, thank you. You needn't bring an old woman anything.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Hm. Thank you... but my teeth and I don't get on with this.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh dear. I'd rather not have that, if it's all the same to you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You already gave me something today. Keep that for yourself.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: An omamori from the shrine... for these old bones?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I'll keep it by the altar, next to my husband's picture. He'd have liked you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A wind chime. I'll hang it where the evening breeze comes in.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A little moon lantern. It'll keep me company on the long nights.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: What a pretty thing. My grandchildren would have fought over it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Furofuki daikon, soft enough for my teeth!

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My mother made it just so, every winter. You cooked this yourself?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Simmered pumpkin, sweet and soft... you remembered what I like?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Did you cook this? It tastes of the old days, and I haven't even opened it yet.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You cooked this? Such a careful hand. I'll have it with my supper.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Home cooking from a young farmer. Thank you, I'll eat it later.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Thank you for cooking, child... but it's a bit rich for an old stomach.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Sit a while. At my age you count the springs, and this one is worth counting.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Lanterns for the ones who've gone ahead. I hung one for my husband by the road.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Set a dumpling out for the moon and it watches over the harvest. So they always said.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Another year closes. You did well, child. The old farm knows it, too.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: In my day you didn't say it out loud. You held out a mizuhiki knot, red and white. Sayo's store still sells them.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Two at the farm on the hill now. Good. A house with one person in it is only a roof.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Put your umbrella up, child, and come in before you get soaked. The tea's already hot.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Rain on the tiles and my husband would doze off in his chair. Lucky man.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Keep clear of the bamboo in this wind, child. It bends, but a falling branch doesn't.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Shutters closed, lamp lit, kettle on. That's how we waited out a storm in my day. Come and sit.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Snow on the tiles again, child. My husband used to sweep the path before I was even up. Mind the step by the gate.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Come in and warm your hands. He always said snow is the sky tucking the fields in for the winter.
